problem: "Temperature is the property that two bodies share when no heat flows between them" is loose: two bodies separated by an adiabatic wall also have no heat flow between them, yet their temperatures can differ. A student can read this as saying any two bodies with no heat exchange are at the same temperature.
fix: Temperature is the property that is equal for two bodies when no net heat flows between them after they are connected by a diathermal wall.

problem: "If θ_A = θ_B, the zeroth law says A and B are in thermal equilibrium" — at that moment A and B are separate and not in contact. The law guarantees that they would be in thermal equilibrium once connected; the sentence as written can confuse a student about what equilibrium means.
fix: If θ_A = θ_B, the zeroth law guarantees that A and B are in thermal equilibrium, so no net heat flows when they are connected by a diathermal wall.

problem: The forward reference "Unit 3, Thermodynamic temperature scale" is plain text, not a chapter link, so on a phone the reader cannot jump to it and may not know which chapter is meant.
fix: Link it: Thermodynamic temperature scale, and drop the unit number.
